questionMetadata.patientPresentation: {patientName}, the pancreatic-oncology research lead, reviews a new radiation-delivery technique after pancreatic tail cancer resection. Its trial is planned around recurrence within two years. The grant writer wants a guaranteed discovery and asks whether 'statistically likely' can be upgraded in the budget justification. The calculation specifies the effect, variability and sampling assumptions before any outcomes are collected.
questionMetadata.stem: What does prospective power describe under the specified alternative in the constructed pancreatic-cancer recurrence trial?

answerChoices.label: Chance of rejection if that alternative is true
answerChoices.rationale: Under the specified true alternative and design assumptions, power is the probability of rejecting the null. It describes how the planned procedure behaves in that situation.

answerChoices.label: Chance that a statistically positive result is true
answerChoices.rationale: This reverses what is conditioned on. Power assumes an alternative to evaluate rejection, rather than estimating whether a statistically positive conclusion is true.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This reverses what is conditioned on. Power assumes an alternative to evaluate rejection, rather than estimating whether a statistically positive conclusion is true.

answerChoices.label: Chance that the null hypothesis itself is true
answerChoices.rationale: The plan does not assign a probability to the null hypothesis being true. It calculates a rejection probability under the specified alternative.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The plan does not assign a probability to the null hypothesis being true. It calculates a rejection probability under the specified alternative.

answerChoices.label: Chance of nonrejection if that alternative is true
answerChoices.rationale: Nonrejection under a true alternative describes a type II error probability. Power instead concerns rejection under that alternative.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Nonrejection under a true alternative describes a type II error probability. Power instead concerns rejection under that alternative.

questionMetadata.explanation: Planned power is the chance of rejecting the null under the specified true alternative and design assumptions. It is not the truth probability of a positive result.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Power is the probability that the analysis rejects the null if the specified alternative is true, under the planned design assumptions. It is a statement about a procedure operating in that situation. Remember the direction of conditioning: it does not give the probability that a positive study conclusion or the alternative itself is true.

questionMetadata.patientPresentation: {patientName}, the skin-oncology journal-club lead, reviews a new topical agent for basal cell carcinoma. The trial evaluates recurrence within two years and does not reject its null model. After seeing the results, authors calculate low power and conclude the agent has no effect. The team is reviewing that conclusion alongside the reported effect estimate and uncertainty.
questionMetadata.stem: Which statement is justified when the constructed basal-cell-carcinoma recurrence trial fails to reject its null and reports low post-hoc power?

answerChoices.label: Post-hoc power does not prove no effect
answerChoices.rationale: A low post-hoc calculation does not establish that the effect is exactly absent. Power is conditional on a specified alternative, rather than a truth probability for the null.

answerChoices.label: Low post-hoc power favors an absent effect
answerChoices.rationale: The later calculation does not make the no-effect conclusion valid. Neither low post-hoc power nor nonrejection supplies proof of an absent effect.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The later calculation does not make the no-effect conclusion valid. Neither low post-hoc power nor nonrejection supplies proof of an absent effect.

answerChoices.label: Post-hoc power gives the probability of the null
answerChoices.rationale: Power does not assign a probability to the null hypothesis. It concerns rejection behavior under a specified alternative.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Power does not assign a probability to the null hypothesis. It concerns rejection behavior under a specified alternative.

answerChoices.label: The observed p-value is the study's achieved power
answerChoices.rationale: A p-value concerns observed-or-more-extreme data under a null model; power concerns rejection under an alternative. They are different conditional quantities.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A p-value concerns observed-or-more-extreme data under a null model; power concerns rejection under an alternative. They are different conditional quantities.

questionMetadata.explanation: Low post-hoc power does not prove no effect. It neither gives the probability of the null nor makes the observed p-value equal to power.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Power describes rejection probability under a specified alternative, not the probability that a hypothesis is true. A low post-hoc power calculation after nonrejection does not establish an exactly absent effect. Remember that a second conditional calculation cannot transform the first result into proof of equality or supply the effect size missing from this exercise.

answerChoices.label: Spread the change and monitor other clinics

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The results apply to the local test. Spreading immediately to other clinics goes beyond that scope instead of testing the next setting.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The supplied favorable aim and balancing findings support local action. Repeating the identical pilot without acting does not use the stated learning.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The findings identify no feature requiring revision before local adoption. Adaptation needs a reason in the learning, rather than a change for its own sake.

questionMetadata.teachingPoint: The Act step turns learning into a decision and a next test. This pathway version met its aim without worsening the balancing measure, supporting local adoption and a linked next cycle. Keep the scope of action tied to the scope of the evidence: a successful small test does not automatically establish performance at every clinic.

questionMetadata.stem: Which Act-step decision fits the authorized venous-ulcer device pilot when healing is faster but application rework doubles?

answerChoices.label: Adapt device use and retest locally
answerChoices.rationale: Healing improved but rework doubled. Revise device use to address that burden and use the next test to study the adapted version.

answerChoices.label: Adopt device use and monitor application rework

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Adopting this version unchanged accepts the documented worsening of rework. The balancing finding calls for adaptation before adoption.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The target improvement supports retaining and adapting the idea. The supplied findings do not require discarding it instead of addressing the added burden.

answerChoices.label: Repeat device use without revising the process

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Repeating the same device unchanged does not respond to the increased rework already observed. The next cycle should use that learning.

This device shortened wound-closure time but doubled rework, so adapt its use and retest rather than adopting the current version unchanged. The Act step can preserve a promising idea while changing the part that caused trouble. Learning should change the next cycle.

answerChoices.rationale: The patient lacks the clinical information needed to choose. Discuss the intervention's relevant risks, benefits, and alternatives, including foregoing it, in an understandable conversation.

questionMetadata.explanation: The missing step is an understandable discussion of the intervention, risks, benefits, and alternatives. Confirming a signature or willingness alone does not fill those information gaps.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Informed consent helps a person understand the intervention, its relevant risks and benefits, and alternatives including declining, so the person can choose voluntarily. Remember: document the conversation, rather than substituting a document for it.

Information has been provided, but a companion threatens to withhold transportation unless the patient signs. In private, the patient says the study is unwanted. Testing has not started, and there is time to discuss the patient's own choice.
questionMetadata.stem: With qualified interpretation in place, how should the team respond when {patientName} privately declines nonurgent manometry after a companion threatens to withhold transportation unless the patient signs?

answerChoices.label: Pause and support the patient's voluntary choice
answerChoices.rationale: The patient privately says the procedure is unwanted after a threat about transport. Pause the elective process and support a voluntary choice rather than rely on the pressured signature.

answerChoices.label: Ask the patient to confirm consent with the companion
answerChoices.rationale: Asking for confirmation in the companion's presence preserves the setting of pressure. It does not protect the voluntary choice expressed in private.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Asking for confirmation in the companion's presence preserves the setting of pressure. It does not protect the voluntary choice expressed in private.

answerChoices.label: Offer another appointment with the same companion
answerChoices.rationale: A later appointment with the same companion does not itself address the pressure undermining consent. Changing the date is not a voluntariness assessment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A later appointment with the same companion does not itself address the pressure undermining consent. Changing the date is not a voluntariness assessment.

answerChoices.label: Ask the companion to explain the patient's preferences
answerChoices.rationale: The companion's account cannot replace the patient's private expressed preference. Practical support does not give the companion authority to impose the elective choice.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The companion's account cannot replace the patient's private expressed preference. Practical support does not give the companion authority to impose the elective choice.

questionMetadata.explanation: Pause and support the patient's voluntary choice. The private refusal and companion's threat undermine reliance on a pressured signature for an nonurgent study with no urgent need.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Consent requires a voluntary choice as well as information and understanding. A signature obtained under the pressure described here cannot substitute for the patient's expressed preference. Pause the nonurgent process and support a voluntary decision in private. Remember that a companion's wishes do not become the patient's wishes merely because the companion provides practical support.

questionMetadata.stem: How should the team respond to {patientName}'s informed refusal of appendectomy when the stated decision-making abilities are intact?

answerChoices.label: Respect refusal and discuss follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: The patient demonstrates informed understanding, coherent reasoning, and a consistent refusal. Respect that choice and discuss follow-up; surgeon disagreement does not establish incapacity.

answerChoices.label: Request psychiatric clearance before accepting refusal
answerChoices.rationale: The supplied concern is disagreement, not inability to decide. That alone does not establish a need for psychiatric clearance before accepting an informed refusal.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The supplied concern is disagreement, not inability to decide. That alone does not establish a need for psychiatric clearance before accepting an informed refusal.

answerChoices.label: Ask the family to confirm the treatment decision
answerChoices.rationale: The patient's demonstrated abilities support making this decision. Family agreement is not what validates this capable adult's informed refusal.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The patient's demonstrated abilities support making this decision. Family agreement is not what validates this capable adult's informed refusal.

answerChoices.label: Repeat consent counseling until surgery is accepted
answerChoices.rationale: Further counseling can address an unanswered question, but repeating it until agreement replaces the informed choice already demonstrated in this scenario.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Further counseling can address an unanswered question, but repeating it until agreement replaces the informed choice already demonstrated in this scenario.

questionMetadata.explanation: Respect the informed refusal and discuss follow-up. The patient demonstrates the required abilities; the surgeon's disagreement alone does not justify replacing the decision or requiring psychiatric or family approval.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Capacity concerns the decision in front of you and the patient's demonstrated abilities, not agreement with the clinician. This patient understands the options and personal implications, reasons coherently, and communicates a consistent refusal. Respect that informed choice and discuss follow-up. Remember: a recommendation can be reasonable without making disagreement evidence of incapacity.

questionMetadata.stem: What should the team do before elective parathyroid surgery when {patientName} is newly confused and cannot understand the operation despite an earlier consent signature?

answerChoices.label: Pause and assess capacity for this decision

answerChoices.label: Verify the earlier consent and continue preparation

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The earlier signature records an earlier discussion. It does not resolve the patient's new inability to understand the current decision.

answerChoices.label: Obtain a fresh signature after repeating the explanation
answerChoices.rationale: A fresh signature after another repetition does not establish understanding. The patient's present abilities need assessment rather than replacement documentation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A fresh signature after another repetition does not establish understanding. The patient's present abilities need assessment rather than replacement documentation.

answerChoices.label: Ask a relative to approve the procedure first
answerChoices.rationale: A relative's approval first bypasses assessment of the patient's current decision-making abilities. Address the present concern before assuming someone else should decide.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A relative's approval first bypasses assessment of the patient's current decision-making abilities. Address the present concern before assuming someone else should decide.

questionMetadata.explanation: Pause the elective process and assess capacity for the current decision. The earlier form does not resolve new confusion and inability to explain the procedure's purpose.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Capacity can change, so an earlier signature does not answer a present concern about understanding. New confusion and inability to explain this procedure warrant pausing and assessing the current decision. Remember to assess the person now for this choice. A fresh signature or a relative's approval does not replace addressing that concern.

questionMetadata.stem: How should the team assess {patientName}'s refusal of thyroid needle sampling when treated depression is recorded but the stated decision-making abilities are intact?

answerChoices.label: Assess current decision-making abilities
answerChoices.rationale: Assess the demonstrated abilities for this specific decision. Accurate understanding, personal appreciation, coherent reasoning, and a stable choice cannot be dismissed because depression is recorded.

answerChoices.label: Require psychiatric clearance because of depression
answerChoices.rationale: Depression alone does not establish incapacity or a requirement for psychiatric clearance. The actual abilities demonstrated in this discussion matter.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Depression alone does not establish incapacity or a requirement for psychiatric clearance. The actual abilities demonstrated in this discussion matter.

answerChoices.label: Use the family's account of the patient's usual judgment
answerChoices.rationale: Family observations can provide context, but a description of usual judgment does not replace assessing the patient's present abilities for this decision.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Family observations can provide context, but a description of usual judgment does not replace assessing the patient's present abilities for this decision.

answerChoices.label: Judge capacity by agreement with the recommendation
answerChoices.rationale: Agreement with the clinician is not a capacity criterion. A reasoned refusal can demonstrate the required abilities even when the clinician favors revision.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Agreement with the clinician is not a capacity criterion. A reasoned refusal can demonstrate the required abilities even when the clinician favors revision.

questionMetadata.explanation: Judge current abilities for this decision, not depression alone. The patient demonstrates understanding, appreciation, coherent reasoning, and a stable choice, supporting respect for the refusal.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: A diagnosis is not a capacity verdict. Assess understanding, personal appreciation, reasoning, and communication for the actual decision. The described abilities support respecting this refusal despite the history of depression. Remember to examine what the patient can do in this discussion, rather than replacing an individual assessment with a diagnostic label or agreement test.

questionMetadata.stem: How should the team approach {patientName}'s decision about a varicose-vein intervention when mild cognitive impairment is recorded but supported understanding is demonstrated?

answerChoices.label: Support and assess the patient's own decision
answerChoices.rationale: Support understanding and assess the patient's own abilities for vein intervention. The described informed, consistent choice should not be displaced solely by the cognitive diagnosis.

answerChoices.label: Obtain a surrogate's decision because of the diagnosis
answerChoices.rationale: Cognitive impairment does not eliminate capacity for every decision. Seeking a surrogate solely from that label skips the abilities demonstrated after support.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Cognitive impairment does not eliminate capacity for every decision. Seeking a surrogate solely from that label skips the abilities demonstrated after support.

answerChoices.label: Require a family countersignature for this consent
answerChoices.rationale: A family countersignature does not replace assessing the patient's supported understanding and choice. The diagnosis alone does not establish that another person must validate consent.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A family countersignature does not replace assessing the patient's supported understanding and choice. The diagnosis alone does not establish that another person must validate consent.

answerChoices.label: Require formal testing before discussing the choice
answerChoices.rationale: The supplied discussion already demonstrates relevant abilities with support. A blanket testing requirement based on the diagnosis does not address those actual abilities.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The supplied discussion already demonstrates relevant abilities with support. A blanket testing requirement based on the diagnosis does not address those actual abilities.

questionMetadata.explanation: Support and assess the patient's own decision about treatment. Demonstrated understanding after plain-language explanation cannot be dismissed solely because cognitive impairment is recorded.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Cognitive impairment does not remove capacity for every decision. Support understanding and assess the patient's actual abilities for this choice before seeking a substitute decision-maker. Plain language enables an informed, consistent choice. Remember that the diagnosis and the decision are separate questions; a label alone does not transfer authority to family or a surrogate.

questionMetadata.stem: What should guide the authorized surrogate's operative decision for {patientName}'s acute cholecystitis when known patient wishes differ from the surrogate's own preference?

answerChoices.label: Use the patient's known preferences
answerChoices.rationale: Specific prior discussions identify what this patient would choose in these circumstances. Substituted judgment uses those known wishes rather than the surrogate's own preference.

answerChoices.label: Use the surrogate's preferred treatment plan
answerChoices.rationale: The surrogate represents the patient's known perspective. Personally favoring treatment does not justify replacing the patient's specific contrary wishes.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The surrogate represents the patient's known perspective. Personally favoring treatment does not justify replacing the patient's specific contrary wishes.

answerChoices.label: Use the family's agreed treatment preference
answerChoices.rationale: Family agreement does not displace a known patient preference. Counting relatives' choices answers whose plan is popular, rather than what this patient would choose.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Family agreement does not displace a known patient preference. Counting relatives' choices answers whose plan is popular, rather than what this patient would choose.

answerChoices.label: Use the option with the greatest expected benefit
answerChoices.rationale: Best-interest deliberation is the fallback when wishes cannot be determined. Here known preferences supply the patient's perspective rather than leaving it unknown.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Best-interest deliberation is the fallback when wishes cannot be determined. Here known preferences supply the patient's perspective rather than leaving it unknown.

questionMetadata.explanation: Use the patient's known preferences through substituted judgment. The surrogate's own preference does not replace specific prior wishes about these circumstances.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Substituted judgment asks what this patient would choose, using known preferences and values. It does not ask what the surrogate would choose for themselves or what most relatives prefer. Here specific prior wishes are available. Remember that the surrogate represents the patient's perspective; best-interest deliberation is the fallback when that perspective cannot be determined.

questionMetadata.stem: What should guide the authorized surrogate's rectal-prolapse surgical deliberation for {patientName} when prior wishes and relevant values cannot be determined?

answerChoices.label: The patient's benefits and burdens
answerChoices.rationale: The patient's wishes and values remain unknown after reasonable efforts. Best-interest deliberation therefore weighs likely benefits, burdens, and suffering for the patient.

answerChoices.label: The choice most family members would make
answerChoices.rationale: A family majority does not establish the patient's best interests. The supplied standard requires attention to the patient's benefits and burdens.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A family majority does not establish the patient's best interests. The supplied standard requires attention to the patient's benefits and burdens.

answerChoices.label: The option with the longest possible survival
answerChoices.rationale: Possible survival is one consideration, not a complete substitute for weighing benefits, burdens, and suffering. The standard is broader than maximizing duration alone.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Possible survival is one consideration, not a complete substitute for weighing benefits, burdens, and suffering. The standard is broader than maximizing duration alone.

answerChoices.label: The surrogate's preferred treatment for themself
answerChoices.rationale: The surrogate's own treatment preference is not the patient's known preference or a complete assessment of the patient's welfare.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The surrogate's own treatment preference is not the patient's known preference or a complete assessment of the patient's welfare.

questionMetadata.explanation: Use the patient's best interests, weighing benefits and burdens. No prior preferences can be identified, so neither family voting nor the surrogate's personal treatment preference supplies the standard.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: When the patient's preferences and values cannot be determined, consider the patient's best interests, including likely benefits, burdens, and suffering. This differs from substituting the surrogate's personal choice or counting family votes. Remember to look for the patient's perspective first; when it is unavailable, keep the patient's welfare at the center of deliberation.

questionMetadata.stem: What is the appropriate next step when the surrogate's requested kidney-stone evaluation conflicts with {patientName}'s documented wishes and discussion has not resolved the disagreement?

answerChoices.label: Seek ethics support for the conflict
answerChoices.rationale: The request still conflicts with documented wishes despite discussion. Appropriate institutional ethics support addresses that unresolved conflict instead of accepting the surrogate's request automatically.

answerChoices.label: Ask another relative to approve the requested treatment
answerChoices.rationale: Another relative's agreement does not resolve the conflict with the patient's documented wishes. Changing who endorses the plan leaves the same ethical concern.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Another relative's agreement does not resolve the conflict with the patient's documented wishes. Changing who endorses the plan leaves the same ethical concern.

answerChoices.label: Use the surrogate's current request as the final decision
answerChoices.rationale: An authorized surrogate's request is not automatic permission to disregard known patient wishes. The unresolved disagreement calls for appropriate support.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: An authorized surrogate's request is not automatic permission to disregard known patient wishes. The unresolved disagreement calls for appropriate support.

answerChoices.label: Repeat the same family meeting before seeking advice
answerChoices.rationale: The supplied discussion has already failed to resolve the conflict. Repeating it unchanged is not a substitute for seeking the appropriate institutional ethics support.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The supplied discussion has already failed to resolve the conflict. Repeating it unchanged is not a substitute for seeking the appropriate institutional ethics support.

questionMetadata.explanation: Seek appropriate institutional ethics support for the unresolved conflict. The surrogate's request remains inconsistent with documented wishes, and there is time to address it without automatic compliance.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: A surrogate request does not automatically override known patient wishes. When discussion leaves that conflict unresolved, appropriate institutional ethics support can help address it rather than accepting the request by default. Remember to preserve the patient's perspective during disagreement. Substituting a different relative or repeating an unchanged meeting does not itself resolve the ethical conflict.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Limiting discussion to the surrogate's choice ignores the patient's remaining abilities and expressed comfort concerns. Those views still deserve attention.

answerChoices.label: Use the patient's simple preference as the final decision
answerChoices.rationale: A simple preference can inform deliberation without establishing capacity for the complex decision. Participation should not be mistaken for complete final authority.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A simple preference can inform deliberation without establishing capacity for the complex decision. Participation should not be mistaken for complete final authority.

questionMetadata.explanation: Include the patient as abilities allow, while the surrogate makes the complex decision. Remaining comfort concerns and simple preferences still deserve direct attention.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Needing a surrogate for one complex choice does not erase every ability to participate. Include the patient to the extent possible and attend to expressed comfort concerns and preferences, while the surrogate handles the complex decision. Remember that participation and final decision authority are separate; neither exclusion nor substitution of a simple preference fits here.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Suspending first and obtaining routine consent does not replace an individualized resuscitation discussion. An automatic suspension bypasses the patient's preferences.

questionMetadata.explanation: Discuss and document an individualized resuscitation plan with the patient or surrogate and responsible clinicians. An automatic operating-room rule does not replace that review.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: An internal review may clarify remaining uncertainties, but it does not require withholding the verified injury and repair. Known facts and the care plan can be discussed now.

answerChoices.label: Explain the planned care without mentioning the injury

answerChoices.distractorRationale: A forward-looking care plan does not replace an honest account of the verified operative event. The patient has asked why the operation changed.

questionMetadata.explanation: Explain the verified unintended injury, its repair, known implications and continuing care plan. An incomplete account or unfinished internal review does not justify concealing known facts.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Honest disclosure explains the verified error, its known implications and the steps taken to address it. answerChoices.label: Explain known facts, uncertainty, and next steps
answerChoices.rationale: State the confirmed loss, current uncertainty, and care and investigation plan. This separates verified facts from the unverified courier theory.

answerChoices.label: Explain the likely courier cause and offer a replacement plan
answerChoices.rationale: The proposed courier explanation remains a theory. Presenting it as the cause replaces acknowledged uncertainty with unverified blame.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The proposed courier explanation remains a theory. Presenting it as the cause replaces acknowledged uncertainty with unverified blame.

answerChoices.label: Wait for a cause to be established before discussing the loss
answerChoices.rationale: A cause need not be established before explaining the known loss. The team can disclose verified facts while acknowledging the investigation is incomplete.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A cause need not be established before explaining the known loss. The team can disclose verified facts while acknowledging the investigation is incomplete.

answerChoices.label: Discuss replacement sampling and defer the reason for it
answerChoices.rationale: A plan for further sampling cannot replace explaining the verified loss and uncertainty. The exercise also does not establish that a specific repeat procedure is always required.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A plan for further sampling cannot replace explaining the verified loss and uncertainty. The exercise also does not establish that a specific repeat procedure is always required.

questionMetadata.explanation: Explain the confirmed loss, what remains uncertain, and the care and investigation plan. Do not state the courier theory as fact or withhold the known loss until the investigation is complete.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Honest disclosure separates verified facts from theories. You can explain a confirmed loss while its cause is still under investigation, acknowledging uncertainty and describing the care and investigation plan. Remember that uncertainty is information to disclose, not a gap to fill with blame. The known fact is specimen loss, not the suspected courier explanation.

answerChoices.rationale: Observation by another clinician does not itself resolve the assigned clinician's inability to perform the setup safely. Use available safe coverage and arrange assessment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Observation by another clinician does not itself resolve the assigned clinician's inability to perform the setup safely. Use available safe coverage and arrange assessment.

answerChoices.label: Pause the procedure and ask the clinician to self-assess
answerChoices.rationale: Self-assessment alone does not address the observed inability. The team must protect care and arrange appropriate assessment rather than placing the whole response on the affected clinician.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Self-assessment alone does not address the observed inability. The team must protect care and arrange appropriate assessment rather than placing the whole response on the affected clinician.

answerChoices.label: Recheck performance after a brief rest before arranging help
answerChoices.rationale: Waiting to see whether rest changes performance delays the available protection and assessment. The present unsafe performance, not an established diagnosis, warrants action.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Waiting to see whether rest changes performance delays the available protection and assessment. The present unsafe performance, not an established diagnosis, warrants action.

questionMetadata.explanation: Arrange safe coverage and appropriate assessment for the clinician. The observed inability requires action, but the behavior alone does not establish its cause.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Observable inability to practice safely calls for patient protection and appropriate assessment, even before the cause is known. Arrange safe coverage and help for the clinician rather than assuming intoxication or relying only on self-assessment. Remember to act on the demonstrated performance problem while keeping its cause an open question until appropriately assessed.

questionMetadata.stem: How should the team respond to credible clinician-confusion concerns that may compromise {patientName}'s duodenal-biopsy follow-up?

answerChoices.label: Arrange assessment and appropriate safety reporting
answerChoices.rationale: Documented confusion that could compromise care warrants assessment, appropriate reporting, and patient protection while supporting the colleague. A final cause is not required to start that response.

answerChoices.label: Arrange peer coaching and recheck performance at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Coaching alone treats the concern as a routine skills issue without addressing the documented confusion, appropriate assessment, or safety reporting.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Coaching alone treats the concern as a routine skills issue without addressing the documented confusion, appropriate assessment, or safety reporting.

answerChoices.label: Transfer the follow-up and await an impairment diagnosis
answerChoices.rationale: Transferring follow-up may protect that task, but waiting for a diagnosis omits the appropriate assessment and reporting response to the current credible concern.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Transferring follow-up may protect that task, but waiting for a diagnosis omits the appropriate assessment and reporting response to the current credible concern.

answerChoices.label: Ask the clinician to explain the missed instructions first
answerChoices.rationale: The clinician's account may inform assessment, but requesting an explanation first must not replace protection and the appropriate response to documented confusion.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The clinician's account may inform assessment, but requesting an explanation first must not replace protection and the appropriate response to documented confusion.

questionMetadata.explanation: Arrange assessment, appropriate safety reporting, and protection of follow-up while supporting the clinician. Concealment or waiting for a diagnosis leaves the documented practice concern unaddressed.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Credible concerns about unsafe practice need patient protection, appropriate assessment, and reporting suited to the setting, alongside support for the colleague. Waiting for a final diagnosis does not resolve the care concern. Remember that protecting reputation cannot replace a safety response; use observed evidence without inventing the cause or treating reporting as a diagnosis.

questionMetadata.stem: What should determine the clinician's fitness to conduct {patientName}'s fissure-treatment consultation when a disability is accommodated and actual performance is safe?

answerChoices.label: Actual ability to perform the care safely
answerChoices.rationale: The relevant issue is actual safe performance, including appropriate accommodations. The scenario establishes that ability and supplies no performance concern.

answerChoices.label: The clinician's diagnosis and expected disease course
answerChoices.rationale: A diagnosis and its expected course are not by themselves a finding of inability to perform this care safely. The actual relevant duties and performance matter.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A diagnosis and its expected course are not by themselves a finding of inability to perform this care safely. The actual relevant duties and performance matter.

answerChoices.label: The clinician's ability without workplace accommodations
answerChoices.rationale: Excluding accommodations changes the supplied assessment. Safe performance with appropriate accommodations is relevant to whether the clinician can perform the duties.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Excluding accommodations changes the supplied assessment. Safe performance with appropriate accommodations is relevant to whether the clinician can perform the duties.

answerChoices.label: The patient's comfort with the clinician's appearance
answerChoices.rationale: Appearance or patient discomfort about it does not establish unsafe practice. The scenario supplies safe performance and no observed concern to support that inference.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Appearance or patient discomfort about it does not establish unsafe practice. The scenario supplies safe performance and no observed concern to support that inference.

questionMetadata.explanation: Use actual ability to perform the relevant care safely, including appropriate accommodations. The supplied safe performance does not support treating visible disability itself as impairment.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Disability and inability to practice safely are different questions. Judge the clinician's actual performance of the relevant duties, including appropriate accommodations. Here safe performance is established and no performance concern exists. Remember to assess the relevant work rather than using appearance, a diagnosis, or ability without accommodations as a substitute for that assessment.

questionMetadata.stem: How should the team respond when the clinician assigned to {patientName}'s dialysis-access assessment reports inability to concentrate safely and requests relief?

answerChoices.label: Arrange safe coverage and appropriate assistance
answerChoices.rationale: Arrange the available safe coverage and appropriate assistance. The clinician has recognized a current inability to concentrate safely and asked for relief before the procedure.

answerChoices.label: Reassign demanding tasks and have the clinician continue

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Reassigning only demanding tasks still requires practice despite the stated inability to concentrate safely. It does not provide the requested relief and available coverage.

answerChoices.label: Offer a short rest before considering relief from duty
answerChoices.rationale: A rest trial postpones relief despite the clinician's stated inability and available coverage. Support the request rather than requiring further unsafe practice to demonstrate it.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A rest trial postpones relief despite the clinician's stated inability and available coverage. Support the request rather than requiring further unsafe practice to demonstrate it.

answerChoices.label: Cancel the visit and defer assistance to occupational health
answerChoices.rationale: Qualified coverage is available, so cancellation does not use that option. Deferring assistance also misses the colleague's current request for help.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Qualified coverage is available, so cancellation does not use that option. Deferring assistance also misses the colleague's current request for help.

questionMetadata.explanation: Arrange safe coverage and appropriate assistance now. The clinician has identified inability to concentrate safely, and qualified replacement care is available before the clinical consultation begins.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: A clinician who recognizes inability to practice safely should be supported in obtaining coverage and appropriate assistance. Here that concern is already expressed and qualified coverage is available. Remember to respond before an unsafe performance is required to prove the problem. Patient protection and help for the clinician belong in the same response.

questionMetadata.stem: What should the team explain when {patientName} is told that ordinary gastric-GIST care depends on joining an optional new-biologic study?

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment does not forfeit ordinary care
answerChoices.rationale: This study is optional and not required for ordinary care. Clarify that declining enrollment does not forfeit that care, so the invitation can be considered voluntarily.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment requires transfer to another clinic
answerChoices.rationale: Requiring transfer would impose a loss of ordinary care for declining this optional study. The scenario gives no basis for making that care contingent on enrollment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Requiring transfer would impose a loss of ordinary care for declining this optional study. The scenario gives no basis for making that care contingent on enrollment.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment postpones the surgical consultation
answerChoices.rationale: Postponing the ordinary consultation because enrollment is declined still makes care conditional on joining. That conflicts with voluntary choice in this setting.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Postponing the ordinary consultation because enrollment is declined still makes care conditional on joining. That conflicts with voluntary choice in this setting.

answerChoices.label: Declining enrollment limits access to routine follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Limiting routine follow-up uses ordinary care to pressure enrollment. The optional study is not required for that care.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Limiting routine follow-up uses ordinary care to pressure enrollment. The optional study is not required for that care.

questionMetadata.explanation: Clarify that declining this optional study does not forfeit ordinary clinic care. The recruiter's stated condition is inconsistent with voluntary participation in a study not required for that care.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Research participation must be voluntary. When a study is optional and not required for ordinary care, declining it should not forfeit that care. Remember to separate the clinical care decision from the research invitation. Making enrollment a condition of routine care pressures the patient instead of supporting an independent choice about participation.

questionMetadata.stem: What is needed before additional research-only tissue sampling when {patientName} has consented only to a clinical endoscopic examination for Barrett esophagus?

answerChoices.label: Complete an appropriate research consent process
answerChoices.rationale: The additional procedure is research-only and was not discussed in the treatment consent. Address its purpose, added procedure, and voluntary choice through appropriate research consent and oversight.

answerChoices.label: Extend the clinical consent to cover the extra sampling
answerChoices.rationale: Clinical consent does not expand automatically to an additional undisclosed research procedure. Extending its label does not supply the missing research discussion or applicable oversight.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Clinical consent does not expand automatically to an additional undisclosed research procedure. Extending its label does not supply the missing research discussion or applicable oversight.

answerChoices.label: Use a signed research form as the entire consent process
answerChoices.rationale: A signed research form alone is not the entire consent process. The participant needs the relevant understandable discussion and voluntary choice for the added activity.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A signed research form alone is not the entire consent process. The participant needs the relevant understandable discussion and voluntary choice for the added activity.

answerChoices.label: Ask the treating surgeon to authorize the extra sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The surgeon's approval is not the patient's research permission. It does not replace the appropriate consent process and applicable oversight.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The surgeon's approval is not the patient's research permission. It does not replace the appropriate consent process and applicable oversight.

questionMetadata.explanation: Complete the appropriate research consent process and applicable oversight before the additional sampling. The clinical-treatment signature does not automatically cover this undisclosed research-only procedure.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Consent to treatment does not automatically authorize an additional research-only procedure. The research purpose, added procedure, and voluntary choice need appropriate research consent and applicable oversight. A signature has a scope: adding a research activity requires addressing that activity, rather than extending the clinical form by assumption or treating another form as the conversation.

questionMetadata.stem: What should research consent explain when {patientName} expects personally selected treatment in a desmoid-agent trial whose protocol uses random allocation?

answerChoices.label: Assignment is random and benefit is uncertain
answerChoices.rationale: The approved protocol assigns randomly and guarantees no better arm. Clarifying both points corrects the expectation of personally selected treatment with assured benefit.

answerChoices.label: Assignment is clinical and benefit is individualized
answerChoices.rationale: The protocol does not use individualized clinical selection. This wording preserves the patient's mistaken expectation instead of explaining random allocation and uncertain benefit.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The protocol does not use individualized clinical selection. This wording preserves the patient's mistaken expectation instead of explaining random allocation and uncertain benefit.

answerChoices.label: Assignment is random and benefit is established
answerChoices.rationale: Random assignment is correct, but established benefit is not. No arm is guaranteed better in the supplied protocol.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Random assignment is correct, but established benefit is not. No arm is guaranteed better in the supplied protocol.

answerChoices.label: Assignment is chosen and benefit is uncertain
answerChoices.rationale: Uncertainty about benefit is correct, but assignment is not chosen by the surgeon or participant. The protocol uses random allocation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Uncertainty about benefit is correct, but assignment is not chosen by the surgeon or participant. The protocol uses random allocation.

questionMetadata.explanation: Explain that assignment is random and benefit uncertain. The protocol does not let the surgeon select a personally best arm or guarantee that an arm will be better.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Research consent needs a clear account of allocation and uncertainty. This protocol assigns arms randomly; the surgeon does not choose a personally best arm, and benefit is not guaranteed. Remember to distinguish a research protocol from individually selected treatment. Understanding assignment helps the patient choose whether to join, not a detail for after enrollment.

questionMetadata.stem: How should the team respond to {patientName}'s request to leave an optional hidradenitis-agent study when unrelated ordinary appointments are threatened?

answerChoices.label: Support withdrawal and preserve ordinary follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Support the voluntary withdrawal and discuss ordinary follow-up separately. Unrelated care must not be used as leverage to require continued research participation.

answerChoices.label: Defer withdrawal until the remaining study visits are complete
answerChoices.rationale: Requiring completion of remaining visits before withdrawal makes continued participation compulsory. That does not respect the voluntary withdrawal request.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Requiring completion of remaining visits before withdrawal makes continued participation compulsory. That does not respect the voluntary withdrawal request.

answerChoices.label: Require the investigator's approval before withdrawal
answerChoices.rationale: Investigator permission is not a condition that justifies compelling continued participation. The patient wants to leave a voluntary study.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Investigator permission is not a condition that justifies compelling continued participation. The patient wants to leave a voluntary study.

answerChoices.label: Arrange transfer of ordinary care before allowing withdrawal
answerChoices.rationale: Requiring transfer first still ties ordinary care to continued enrollment. Preserve the unrelated follow-up rather than using its loss to prevent withdrawal.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Requiring transfer first still ties ordinary care to continued enrollment. Preserve the unrelated follow-up rather than using its loss to prevent withdrawal.

questionMetadata.explanation: Support withdrawal and preserve ordinary clinical follow-up. The threatened cancellation of unrelated care must not be used to compel continued participation in a voluntary study.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Voluntary participation includes being able to withdraw without coercive loss of ordinary care. Discuss ongoing clinical follow-up separately from whether research continues. Remember that stopping research participation and stopping clinical care are different choices. Neither completing unwanted study visits nor obtaining investigator permission should be used as the price of preserving unrelated follow-up.

answerChoices.rationale: A journal plan alone does not determine research classification. The institution must consider the project's purpose, design, and applicable definitions.

answerChoices.label: Publication intent establishes a generalizable research aim
answerChoices.rationale: Wanting publication is not by itself proof of a generalizable research aim. The actual purpose and activities still require assessment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Wanting publication is not by itself proof of a generalizable research aim. The actual purpose and activities still require assessment.

answerChoices.label: Journal submission determines the need for research review

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Journal submission is a publishing step, not the institutional determination of applicable research requirements. The project cannot be classified from that step alone.

answerChoices.label: Peer review determines the project's research classification
answerChoices.rationale: Peer review evaluates a submission; it does not by itself classify the underlying activity under applicable research definitions.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Peer review evaluates a submission; it does not by itself classify the underlying activity under applicable research definitions.

questionMetadata.explanation: Explain that publication plans alone do not define research. Appropriate institutional assessment must consider the project's purpose, design, and applicable definitions rather than its intended journal destination.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Publication intent alone does not determine whether an activity is research. Classification depends on its purpose, design, and applicable definitions, assessed through the appropriate institution. Remember that where a report may appear is different from what the project does. This exercise does not establish an exemption or replace assessment with a publishing plan.

Susan agrees; there is time to explain.

approvedInstantiationProfiles.presentation: Lily Walker, a 6-year-old girl, visits the clinic with her mother, Susan Walker, who remains in the same room throughout the visit. An intermittent groin bulge prompts nonurgent hernia assessment. Lily asks what the examination involves. 'Mum has already answered, but she hasn't done the examining,' she says. Susan agrees; there is time to explain.

questionMetadata.stem: Which communication approach should be used before Lily Walker's nonurgent groin examination when her mother agrees but Lily has questions?

answerChoices.label: Explain to Lily and invite her participation
answerChoices.rationale: Lily has questions before a nonurgent examination. Explain in terms she can understand and invite her participation, while keeping Susan involved rather than treating her agreement as the whole discussion.

answerChoices.label: Explain to Susan and begin the examination
answerChoices.rationale: Susan's agreement does not answer Lily's questions or provide the child's own developmentally appropriate participation before this nonurgent examination.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Susan's agreement does not answer Lily's questions or provide the child's own developmentally appropriate participation before this nonurgent examination.

answerChoices.label: Accept Lily's silence and begin the examination
answerChoices.rationale: Silence does not establish meaningful participation. Lily has asked what will happen and needs an understandable explanation and an opportunity for questions.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Silence does not establish meaningful participation. Lily has asked what will happen and needs an understandable explanation and an opportunity for questions.

answerChoices.label: Postpone Lily's involvement until she is older
answerChoices.rationale: Participation can match Lily's present understanding. A universal older-age requirement would postpone the explanation and invitation this nonurgent visit permits.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Participation can match Lily's present understanding. A universal older-age requirement would postpone the explanation and invitation this nonurgent visit permits.

questionMetadata.explanation: Explain the examination directly to Lily, invite questions, and seek developmentally appropriate assent with her mother involved. Her participation and legal consent authority are separate considerations.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Assent means inviting the child's developmentally appropriate participation, not treating a parent's agreement as the end of discussion. Explain the examination in language Lily can understand, invite questions, and seek her participation with Susan involved. Remember to include the child directly. This ethical approach does not establish a universal rule about legal consent authority.

questionMetadata.patientPresentation: Ruby Anderson, an 11-year-old girl, visits the clinic with her father, Thomas Anderson, who remains in the same room throughout the visit. Ruby is well with small mobile reactive cervical nodes and no concerning findings. At this nonurgent visit, she asks what observation means and wants the plan explained to her. Thomas asks whether his agreement is enough.

approvedInstantiationProfiles.presentation: Ruby Anderson, an 11-year-old girl, visits the clinic with her father, Thomas Anderson, who remains in the same room throughout the visit. Ruby is well with small mobile reactive cervical nodes and no concerning findings. At this nonurgent visit, she asks what observation means and wants the plan explained to her. Thomas asks whether his agreement is enough.

questionMetadata.stem: Which communication approach should be used for Ruby Anderson's nonurgent neck-node observation plan when her father agrees but she wants the plan explained?

answerChoices.label: Explain to Ruby and invite her questions
answerChoices.rationale: Ruby explicitly says she does not understand. Address her directly with an appropriate explanation and invitation for questions and assent, while retaining her father's involvement.

answerChoices.label: Confirm with Thomas and begin the clinic plan
answerChoices.rationale: Thomas's agreement does not resolve Ruby's stated lack of understanding. Confirming only his view leaves the child's own participation unanswered.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Thomas's agreement does not resolve Ruby's stated lack of understanding. Confirming only his view leaves the child's own participation unanswered.

answerChoices.label: Accept Ruby's silence and begin the clinic plan
answerChoices.rationale: Eventual silence does not establish understanding. The response should give Ruby a meaningful opportunity to understand the plan and express questions or views.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Eventual silence does not establish understanding. The response should give Ruby a meaningful opportunity to understand the plan and express questions or views.

answerChoices.label: Postpone Ruby's involvement until she is older
answerChoices.rationale: Participation should match Ruby's understanding now. Deferring all involvement to a fixed older age bypasses the understandable discussion she is requesting.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Participation should match Ruby's understanding now. Deferring all involvement to a fixed older age bypasses the understandable discussion she is requesting.

questionMetadata.explanation: Include Ruby directly, explain the plan understandably, and invite questions and developmentally appropriate assent with her father involved. Her ethical participation and legal consent authority remain separate considerations.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: A child's voice can be missed even when a parent is engaged and supportive. Explain the plan directly to Ruby, check understanding, and invite her questions and developmentally appropriate assent with Thomas involved. Remember that parental agreement and child participation address different needs. This ethical participation does not settle jurisdiction-specific legal consent authority.

questionMetadata.stem: Which examination protocol should be ordered next for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Hepatobiliary scintigraphy assessing gallbladder filling
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent local inflammatory findings call for assessment of gallbladder filling/cystic-duct obstruction despite the ultrasound components.

answerChoices.label: Hepatobiliary scintigraphy measuring stimulated ejection fraction
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Confuses evaluation of chronic gallbladder emptying with evaluation of the acute inflammatory presentation.

answerChoices.label: MR cholangiopancreatography assessing the extrahepatic ducts
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Prioritizes a duct-stone question over the gallbladder question suggested by persistent local signs; it is not a claim that MRI is never appropriate after ultrasound.

questionMetadata.explanation: The clinical findings maintain concern for acute gallbladder inflammation. A filling study addresses cystic-duct obstruction; a stimulated ejection-fraction study addresses a different physiologic question. MRCP is a duct-focused protocol, not a universal substitute for either. Interpret any scan with preparation and technical limitations in mind.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: The clinical findings maintain concern for acute gallbladder inflammation. questionMetadata.stem: Which evaluation plan should guide {patientName}'s next visit?

answerChoices.label: Breast assessment and medication review
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes a focal concerning component alongside a plausible systemic explanation for the expressed bilateral secretion; an elevated prolactin does not explain away the focal episodes.

answerChoices.label: Medication review and symptom reassessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Over-unifies the observed patterns under a real prolactin-raising medicine and postpones assessment of the focal component.

answerChoices.label: Endocrine assessment and medication review
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Overweights the laboratory abnormality and treats it as a sufficient explanation for all of the breast observations.

questionMetadata.explanation: A medication-related prolactin rise can account for bilateral secretion, while spontaneous unilateral duct discharge still warrants breast-local assessment. The two patterns can coexist; do not assume one systemic finding explains both.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: A medication-related prolactin rise can account for bilateral secretion, while spontaneous unilateral duct discharge still warrants breast-local assessment. The two patterns can coexist; do not assume one systemic finding explains both.

questionMetadata.stem: Which initial imaging pathway should be arranged for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Mammography and targeted ultrasound
answerChoices.rationale: Matches initial symptomatic breast assessment at this adult age after interpretation of the focal discharge component.

answerChoices.label: Contrast-enhanced MRI and targeted ultrasound
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Moves an advanced problem-solving modality into the initial pathway without a preceding conventional assessment.

answerChoices.label: Mammography and contrast-enhanced MRI
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Substitutes an advanced examination for the targeted ultrasound component of the initial workup.

questionMetadata.explanation: The focal discharge history requires a symptomatic imaging pathway. The initial combination at this age is mammography with targeted ultrasound; MRI can have a subsequent problem-solving role.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: The focal discharge history requires a symptomatic imaging pathway. The initial combination at this age is mammography with targeted ultrasound; MRI can have a subsequent problem-solving role.

questionMetadata.stem: Which combined medication plan should be agreed with {patientName}'s surgical team?

answerChoices.label: Continue ART; plan titrated intravenous midazolam with respiratory monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Preserves ART continuity and uses the route for which monitored, individualized midazolam administration can be considered with a boosted regimen.

answerChoices.label: Continue ART; plan oral midazolam with respiratory monitoring
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Preserves continuity but treats monitoring as sufficient to make the contraindicated oral combination acceptable.

answerChoices.label: Interrupt ART; plan titrated intravenous midazolam with respiratory monitoring
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Changes a complete regimen unnecessarily instead of coordinating the interacting procedural medicine.

answerChoices.label: Interrupt ART; plan oral midazolam with respiratory monitoring
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Both interrupts treatment and assumes an unspecified interruption makes the oral interaction acceptable.

questionMetadata.explanation: Coordinate ART continuity and procedural medicines with the HIV/anesthesia teams. Oral midazolam should not be coadministered with a boosted protease-inhibitor regimen; parenteral use needs appropriate monitoring, individualized titration and consideration of dose reduction. No interruption or washout interval is assumed here.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Coordinate ART continuity and procedural medicines with the HIV/anesthesia teams. Oral midazolam should not be coadministered with a boosted protease-inhibitor regimen; parenteral use needs appropriate monitoring, individualized titration and consideration of dose reduction. questionMetadata.stem: Which instruction best fits {patientName}'s sedation plan?

answerChoices.label: Consider smaller midazolam increments with monitored titration
answerChoices.rationale: Applies the boosted-regimen interaction to repeat parenteral dosing, retaining appropriate medical monitoring rather than forbidding all midazolam use.

answerChoices.label: Consider standard midazolam increments with monitored titration
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Fails to account for the expected increase in exposure when planning repeated doses.

answerChoices.label: Consider omitting ritonavir; use standard increments with monitored titration
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Assumes uncoordinated booster omission is an adequate interaction-management strategy without an established interruption plan.

questionMetadata.explanation: Boosted protease-inhibitor treatment can increase midazolam exposure. Parenteral use can be considered with appropriate monitoring and medical management; dose reduction deserves particular consideration when more than one dose is planned. An unsupervised ART change is not a substitute for that coordination.

questionMetadata.stem: Which motility diagnosis best accounts for {patientName}'s combined study findings?

answerChoices.label: Achalasia
answerChoices.rationale: Integrates the body-pressure/contraction distinction with the appropriate junction-relaxation criterion; an apparent pressure event is not automatically normal peristalsis.

answerChoices.label: Esophagogastric junction outflow obstruction
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Represents a competing motility classification; check whether its relaxation and true-peristalsis requirements fit all of the reported observations.

answerChoices.label: Distal esophageal spasm
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Represents a competing motility classification; check whether its relaxation and true-peristalsis requirements fit all of the reported observations.

questionMetadata.explanation: Simultaneous pressurization does not establish a propagated contraction. Integrating absent true peristalsis with impaired junction relaxation supports achalasia rather than preserved-peristalsis outflow obstruction or spasm.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Simultaneous pressurization does not establish a propagated contraction. Integrating absent true peristalsis with impaired junction relaxation supports achalasia rather than preserved-peristalsis outflow obstruction or spasm.

questionMetadata.stem: Which initial imaging plan should be arranged for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Groin ultrasound with standing and Valsalva
answerChoices.rationale: Tests the intermittent mechanical observation rather than assuming the coexisting musculoskeletal pain explains it.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic MRI with hip and adductor assessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Investigates the genuine competing musculoskeletal explanation, but is not the initial dynamic groin assessment in this setting.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic CT with abdominal-wall and groin assessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Can show anatomy, but a routine cross-sectional survey does not provide the usual first dynamic assessment of an intermittent lump.

questionMetadata.explanation: The pain findings and intermittent swelling need not have the same explanation. Initial dynamic groin ultrasound can evaluate a lump that disappears at rest. Persistent uncertainty after an adequate assessment can require further investigation; MRI is not dismissed as an invalid alternative in every occult-hernia pathway.

answerChoices.rationale: Integrates the demonstrated lesion with repeated functional limitation, while leaving the actual operation and shared decision to assessment.

answerChoices.label: Watchful waiting with an individualized symptom-triggered review
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Applies an approach more suited to selected minimally symptomatic patients despite the supplied recurring activity limitation.

answerChoices.label: Support-garment management with an individualized scheduled review
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Offers symptom support but treats it as the main long-term strategy despite repeated functional limitation.

questionMetadata.stem: Which regional imaging plan should be obtained before {patientName}'s operation?

answerChoices.label: Neck ultrasound surveying central and lateral nodal compartments
answerChoices.rationale: Integrates the follicular-cell malignancy pattern with the missing regional assessment; ultrasound supplies the initial compartment survey and can direct further sampling.

answerChoices.label: Contrast neck CT surveying central and lateral nodal compartments
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Is a useful adjunct for selected extensive or invasive disease, rather than the initial replacement for the routine sonographic compartment assessment here.

answerChoices.label: FDG PET-CT surveying central and lateral nodal compartments
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Mistakes an advanced metabolic examination for the initial regional mapping study in this newly evaluated differentiated thyroid malignancy.

questionMetadata.explanation: The cytology supports papillary thyroid carcinoma. Initial preoperative cervical ultrasound evaluates the primary and regional nodal compartments; cross-sectional or metabolic imaging has additional indications, not an automatic first role from this record.

questionMetadata.stem: Which management plan should be initiated for {patientName}'s stoma problem?

answerChoices.label: Hospital surgical assessment with intravenous resuscitation
answerChoices.rationale: Integrates the obstructive symptoms and nonreduction; visible red bowel does not establish an uncomplicated prolapse.

answerChoices.label: Osmotic stoma reduction with supervised outpatient reassessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Applies a conservative uncomplicated-prolapse strategy to a presentation with obstructive symptoms.

answerChoices.label: Sedated manual reduction with supervised outpatient reassessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Focuses on achieving reduction without first addressing the concerning obstruction/acute surgical assessment requirement.

questionMetadata.explanation: Vomiting, marked output reduction and a nonreducible prolapse warrant hospital surgical assessment and supportive resuscitation. Red bowel is not proof of ischemia, but neither does it justify treating the presentation as uncomplicated.

answerChoices.label: Sentinel lymph node mapping and biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: Interprets the primary depth and clinically uninvolved basin, rather than treating reassuring node imaging as exclusion of microscopic involvement.

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided biopsy of an imaged regional node

questionMetadata.stem: Which motility diagnosis best accounts for {patientName}'s returned study?

answerChoices.rationale: Integrates failed propagation with the abnormal junction-relaxation measurement rather than relying on either finding alone.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The small accessible lesion can be completely sampled rather than selecting one potentially unrepresentative edge.

questionMetadata.stem: Which test should be completed before {patientName}'s adrenal biopsy?

answerChoices.label: Plasma free metanephrines
answerChoices.rationale: Evaluates the catecholamine-related hazard before the planned invasive sampling.

answerChoices.label: Overnight dexamethasone suppression
answerChoices.rationale: Selects cortisol assessment from the adrenal hormonal workup rather than evaluating catecholamine secretion.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Selects cortisol assessment from the adrenal hormonal workup rather than evaluating catecholamine secretion.

answerChoices.label: Plasma aldosterone-renin ratio
answerChoices.rationale: Selects a mineralocorticoid workup from a different adrenal decision pathway.

Cortisol or aldosterone evaluation answers different questions.

questionMetadata.stem: Which statistical test is most appropriate for comparing recurrence between the study groups?

answerChoices.label: Fisher exact test
answerChoices.rationale: Interprets the small observed categorical table and the inadequacy of the usual large-sample approximation.

answerChoices.label: Pearson chi-square test
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes independent categorical groups but overlooks the sparse expected-count problem.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Recognizes independent categorical groups but overlooks the sparse expected-count problem.

answerChoices.label: McNemar test
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes a binary outcome but mistakes the two independent groups for paired observations.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Recognizes a binary outcome but mistakes the two independent groups for paired observations.

questionMetadata.explanation: Fisher exact testing fits this small two-by-two table from independent groups. Expected counts derived from the observed margins are too sparse for the usual Pearson approximation in this exercise. McNemar testing would require paired binary observations. The invented counts do not establish clinical efficacy.

questionMetadata.stem: Which measure is calculated by the expression in this ulcer-recurrence report?

answerChoices.label: Odds ratio
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes the ratio of two odds, rather than a direct comparison of probabilities.

answerChoices.label: Risk ratio
answerChoices.rationale: Treats division of odds as though it were division of the probabilities themselves.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Treats division of odds as though it were division of the probabilities themselves.

answerChoices.label: Risk difference
answerChoices.rationale: Confuses a relative comparison with subtraction of the two probabilities.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Confuses a relative comparison with subtraction of the two probabilities.

questionMetadata.explanation: Each p/(1-p) term is an odds. Dividing the two terms produces an odds ratio. A risk ratio divides the probabilities themselves, and a risk difference subtracts them. Similarity in selected settings does not make these measures interchangeable.
questionMetadata.teachingPoint: Each p/(1-p) term is an odds. Dividing the two terms produces an odds ratio. A risk ratio divides the probabilities themselves, and a risk difference subtracts them. Similarity in selected settings does not make these measures interchangeable.

questionMetadata.stem: Which mechanism best explains the recorded end-tidal CO2 change?

answerChoices.rationale: Connects insufflation with a new systemic CO2 load requiring ventilatory clearance.

answerChoices.rationale: Interprets elevated expired CO2 as inspired-gas contamination despite the supplied inspiratory tracing.

questionMetadata.stem: Which diagnosis is best supported by this skin biopsy?

answerChoices.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
answerChoices.rationale: Integrates skin location, morphology and the panel; no single stain alone establishes the diagnosis.

answerChoices.label: Metastatic pulmonary small-cell carcinoma
answerChoices.rationale: Shares small-cell neuroendocrine morphology, making the pattern across CK20 and TTF1 important rather than the word small-cell alone.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Shares small-cell neuroendocrine morphology, making the pattern across CK20 and TTF1 important rather than the word small-cell alone.

answerChoices.label: Primary cutaneous malignant melanoma
answerChoices.rationale: A malignant skin nodule remains plausible initially, but the combined epithelial/neuroendocrine staining favors another lineage.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A malignant skin nodule remains plausible initially, but the combined epithelial/neuroendocrine staining favors another lineage.

answerChoices.label: Primary cutaneous malignant lymphoma
answerChoices.rationale: Small dermal malignant cells can suggest a lymphoid process before the integrated immunophenotype is considered.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Small dermal malignant cells can suggest a lymphoid process before the integrated immunophenotype is considered.

questionMetadata.explanation: The morphology and combined CK20, synaptophysin and TTF1 pattern favor Merkel cell carcinoma among these options. Integrate the panel with the clinical and pathologic assessment.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: This is less concerning than the irregular spiculated combination.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The complete imaging assessment, not one descriptor, determines the final category.
